nodes.title: Sol 5: Gloomy Midpoint
nodes.nasaFactBanner: 2018 LESSON: In 2018, Opportunity went silent while storm winds lifted moisture skyward.
nodes.storyText: Zero solar power for days! Winds lift water vapor skyward. Route watts from your nuclear reactor to keep rocket fuel cold or heat rooms.
nodes.guideTip: The storm is at its halfway point! Hang in there, space explorers!
nodes.novaHint: Check your nuclear watts. Keep the rocket safe without freezing crew rooms.

consequences.text: Sol 4 chilled fuel draws steady power (-5% Power), but calms the crew (+4% Crew Health).
Wearing parkas saved heating power (0% Electricity Conserved!), but heavy coats tire crew (-4% Crew Health).
Cold corridors save heating power (0% Electricity Conserved!), while frosty bulkheads chill crew (-4% Crew Health).
Sleeping rovers saved energy (0% Electricity Conserved!), but losing mobile eyes adds stress (-2% Crew Health).

choiceA.description: Spend electricity to keep return rocket fuel safely frozen.
choiceA.outcomeText: Rocket fuel stays freezing cold! The crew quarters feel chilly.
choiceA.nasaRealDecision: Return rockets store liquid methane at super cold temperatures.
choiceA.nasaFactEmphasis: Tanks need chillers so fuel does not warm up and turn into gas.
choiceA.guideReaction: Fuel chilled! The ticket home is safe and ready.

choiceB.description: Route heat inward for warm showers and healthy muscle stretches.
choiceB.outcomeText: Warm water and stretches bring smiles! Battery reserves dip lower.
choiceB.nasaRealDecision: Astronauts exercise two hours daily to keep bones and muscles strong.
choiceB.nasaFactEmphasis: Zero gravity and cold rooms make muscles feel stiff without exercise.
choiceB.guideReaction: Warm showers! Everyone is stretching and feeling energized.

choiceC.description: Cut heat to outer exercise rooms to save battery power.
choiceC.outcomeText: Batteries stay rock steady! Frost creeps closer along the outer halls.
choiceC.nasaRealDecision: Spacecraft shut down non-vital rooms to protect battery reserves.
choiceC.nasaFactEmphasis: Saving power keeps essential computer clocks and air pumps alive.
choiceC.guideReaction: Blankets on! Conserving power keeps life support running.

nodes.title: Sol 5: Cabin Fever Days
nodes.nasaFactBanner: 2018 LESSON: Mars dust storms trap ground heat for weeks during twilight.
nodes.storyText: Dust keeps trapping heat outside. Five long Martian Sols in dim light make astronauts miss greenhouse crops and sun.
nodes.guideTip: Staying inside for days is tough. Space crews play games to stay cheerful!
nodes.novaHint: Astronaut mood matters. Light and good rest keep your team sharp.

consequences.text: Lowering chillers saved power (0% Electricity Conserved!), but fuel worries stress crew (-4% Crew Health).
Hot meals used power (-4% Power), but kept crew spirits high (+5% Crew Health).
Clean Sol 4 filters keep fresh air flowing quietly (+5% Crew Health).

choiceA.description: Shut off outer bedroom heaters and camp together in command.
choiceA.outcomeText: Turning off bedroom heaters saves power! Crowded rooms make sleep noisy.
choiceA.nasaRealDecision: Crews gather in small, well-insulated cabins to stay warm together.
choiceA.nasaFactEmphasis: Grouping humans together shares natural body warmth efficiently.
choiceA.guideReaction: Campfire style! Cozy together, even if snoring is loud.

choiceB.description: Spend battery power on bright daylight lamps in private bunks.
choiceB.outcomeText: Bright daylight bulbs chase away gloom! Battery meters slide down.
choiceB.nasaRealDecision: Daylight lamps help astronauts regulate circadian sleep cycles.
choiceB.nasaFactEmphasis: Bright full-spectrum light tells the brain when to stay alert.
choiceB.guideReaction: Bright lights! It feels like a sunny spring morning inside.

choiceC.description: Pack astronauts into tight shelter bunks next to the reactor core.
choiceC.outcomeText: Shelter bunks save strong wattage! Stiff bunks leave backs sore.
choiceC.nasaRealDecision: Space habitats include small shielded areas for storm emergencies.
choiceC.nasaFactEmphasis: Thick water walls around storm shelters block cosmic radiation.
choiceC.guideReaction: Shelter bunks locked! Big power saved, but tight sleeping.

nodes.title: Sol 5: Dust Haze Inside
nodes.nasaFactBanner: 2018 LESSON: Curiosity snapped a selfie showing fine dust covering its deck.
nodes.storyText: Just like when haze coated lenses on Curiosity, sticky red grit dims base lamps. No dust devils are clearing panels today.
nodes.guideTip: Curiosity took a photo of itself covered in red dust. Say cheese!
nodes.novaHint: Fine dust irritates lungs. Clean the air before crew stamina drops.

consequences.text: Bypassing clogged filters left fine dust in ducts (-6% Crew Health).
Tethered rover batteries supply power (0% Electricity Conserved!), but tracked grit indoors (-3% Crew Health).
Pressurized airlocks block outdoor dust, protecting breathing (+4% Crew Health).

choiceA.description: Turn on loud medical air scrubbers to strip dust from rooms.
choiceA.outcomeText: Turbines trap the red haze quickly! Scrubbers draw heavy power.
choiceA.nasaRealDecision: Space air filters run multi-stage fans to capture floating dust.
choiceA.nasaFactEmphasis: Electrostatic plates pull charged dust grains right out of air.
choiceA.guideReaction: Vroooom! The big vacuums swallowed all that red dust.

choiceB.description: Save electricity by having crew wear paper filter masks all Sol.
choiceB.outcomeText: Saving power protects the batteries! Itchy masks make crew cough.
choiceB.nasaRealDecision: Astronauts wear masks whenever cabin dust levels rise above normal.
choiceB.nasaFactEmphasis: N95-grade filters stop 95% of airborne mineral particles.
choiceB.guideReaction: Masks on! Power is safe, but noses feel itchy.

choiceC.description: Drive outside rovers to pulse electric shields on outer vents.
choiceC.outcomeText: Rovers sweep outdoor vents clear! Clean air flows back inside.
choiceC.nasaRealDecision: Remote rovers can clear vents without risking astronaut spacewalks.
choiceC.nasaFactEmphasis: Robotic arms perform delicate exterior brush work in toxic air.
choiceC.guideReaction: Good little rovers! They cleaned vents without any spacewalk.

nodes.title: Sol 5: Radio Wait in Blackout
nodes.nasaFactBanner: 2018 LESSON: Earth radio signals take 22 minutes to travel to Mars.
nodes.storyText: Satellites show this is a planet-wide storm! An MRO relay satellite passes overhead across the 22-minute radio delay.
nodes.guideTip: By the time Earth answers, 44 minutes pass! You are in charge here.
nodes.novaHint: You make the calls. Decide whether to spend power on radio or warmth.

consequences.text: Beacon mode saved power (0% Electricity Conserved!), but dark rooms stressed crew (-4% Crew Health).
Orbiter pings used power (-4% Power), but family mail boosted morale (+5% Crew Health).
Auxiliary scrubbers ran smoothly (0% Electricity Conserved!) and kept air fresh (+3% Crew Health).

choiceA.description: Power down deep-space dishes and rec rooms to save electricity.
choiceA.outcomeText: Batteries conserve every watt! Radio silence leaves crew lonely.
choiceA.nasaRealDecision: Cutting radio amplifiers saves dozens of kilowatts during emergencies.
choiceA.nasaFactEmphasis: Deep space transmitters need powerful water-cooled tubes to broadcast.
choiceA.guideReaction: Radios off! Power is guarded, but the room is quiet.

choiceB.description: Spend power warming sleeping bunks and cleaning cabin air.
choiceB.outcomeText: Warm vents ease tired muscles! Battery reserves drop down lower.
choiceB.nasaRealDecision: Comfortable living temperatures help astronauts recover from stress.
choiceB.nasaFactEmphasis: Warm air and good sleep help human immune cells stay active.
choiceB.guideReaction: Warm and cozy! Rest is the best medicine for the crew.

choiceC.description: Use radio dish to send storm readings and download Earth mail.
choiceC.outcomeText: Fresh weather maps and Earth notes cheer everyone! Power drops.
choiceC.nasaRealDecision: Mars orbiters store and forward gigabytes of science data daily.
choiceC.nasaFactEmphasis: High-speed lasers and radio dishes bridge the space gap home.
choiceC.guideReaction: Mail call! Cheerful voices from Earth make hearts light.

nodes.title: Sol 6: Cut Off by Dust
nodes.nasaFactBanner: 2018 LESSON: Storm winds in 100x thinner air carry dust, not physical force.
nodes.storyText: Weeks ago satellites spotted a tiny dust storm. Now thin Martian air cuts you off across a 22-minute radio delay.
nodes.guideTip: Thin air means wind can lift tiny dust, but cannot blow you away!
nodes.novaHint: Six Sols in the dark is tough. Keep communication and drones ready.

consequences.text: Fuel chillers draw power (-4% Power), but safe launch fuel calms crew (+3% Crew Health).
Overcharged cells from Sol 1 still supply backup voltage (+3% Electricity).
Locked chillers save grid power (0% Electricity Conserved!), but chill halls (-3% Crew Health).
Chiller pumps used battery power (-4% Power), but kept fuel tanks ice-cold (+4% Crew Health).
Camping in central hub saved heat (0% Electricity Conserved!), though noise ruined sleep (-4% Crew Health).
Cutting lounge power preserved reserves (0% Electricity Conserved!), but silence felt lonely (-3% Crew Health).

choiceA.description: Spend battery power to send storm readings and stream family voices.
choiceA.outcomeText: Family voices echo across space! Transmitting uses heavy power.
choiceA.nasaRealDecision: Giant antenna dishes on Earth listen for faint signals from Mars.
choiceA.nasaFactEmphasis: Signals take 22 minutes to travel across 150 million miles.
choiceA.guideReaction: Hello Earth! Hearing family voices makes everyone smile warmly.

choiceB.description: Switch off big transmitters so all electricity stays in batteries.
choiceB.outcomeText: Power bars hold completely steady! Silent rooms deepen homesickness.
choiceB.nasaRealDecision: Spacecraft hold radio silence to conserve power during dark flybys.
choiceB.nasaFactEmphasis: Radio transmitters are among the heaviest electrical draws on board.
choiceB.guideReaction: Quiet base! Batteries are safe and sound for tomorrow.

choiceC.description: Fly a tough little drone above dust to see if skies are clearing.
choiceC.outcomeText: The drone spots thinning dust above! Flying the drone uses power.
choiceC.nasaRealDecision: NASA flew the Ingenuity helicopter over 70 times in thin Mars air.
choiceC.nasaFactEmphasis: Drone blades must spin 2,400 times a minute in thin air.
choiceC.guideReaction: Look at the drone fly! It sees blue sky peeking through!

nodes.title: Sol 6: Fresh Veggie Dreams
nodes.nasaFactBanner: 2018 LESSON: One Mars Sol is about 24 hours and 39 minutes long.
nodes.storyText: Six long rounds of a Martian Sol make astronauts crave greenhouse crops! Run the MOXIE oxygen maker or save electricity.
nodes.guideTip: An extra 39 minutes every day adds up! Mars days are slightly longer.
nodes.novaHint: Fresh salad and clean air boost stamina. Balance food with batteries.

consequences.text: Warmed gym gear from Sol 5 kept muscles limber and strong (+4% Crew Health).
Bright daylight lamps restored natural sleep cycles (+5% Crew Health), using power (-4% Power).
Heavy scrubbers cleared red haze (+4% Crew Health), but drew power (-5% Power).

choiceA.description: Cut heater power to outdoor rovers so all energy stays indoors.
choiceA.outcomeText: Outside power drain stops! Rovers sit dark and cold in the grit.
choiceA.nasaRealDecision: Rovers enter deep sleep modes when solar panels cannot charge batteries.
choiceA.nasaFactEmphasis: Warming only critical electronics prevents complete battery drain.
choiceA.guideReaction: Rovers sleeping tight! Every watt is saved for the crew.

choiceB.description: Power up the dish to get breathing tips from flight doctors.
choiceB.outcomeText: Doctors beam back great exercises! Running the transmitter uses power.
choiceB.nasaRealDecision: Flight surgeons on Earth monitor astronaut health 24 hours a day.
choiceB.nasaFactEmphasis: Doctors give personalized advice on nutrition, sleep, and exercise.
choiceB.guideReaction: Doctor orders received! Breathing exercises help everyone relax.

choiceC.description: Turn on purple LED grow-lights so fresh salad plants sprout.
choiceC.outcomeText: Crunchy lettuce grows under purple lights! Grow-lamps draw power.
choiceC.nasaRealDecision: Plants use red and blue light best, making grow-rooms glow purple.
choiceC.nasaFactEmphasis: LED lights give plants energy without wasting heat.
choiceC.guideReaction: Green sprouts! Fresh salad is growing under purple lamps.

nodes.title: Sol 6: Nuclear Core Warning
nodes.nasaFactBanner: 2018 LESSON: Nuclear generators keep humming through total blackout.
nodes.storyText: Just like Curiosity rolled on nuclear power, your nuclear reactor hums! You must also inspect dusty airlock suit doors.
nodes.guideTip: The nuclear reactor is our trusty engine. Treat it with care!
nodes.novaHint: Do not push the reactor too hard. Balance power boost with noise.

consequences.text: Skipping air scrubbers on Sol 5 left itchy dust in bunks (-5% Crew Health).
Tight shelter bunks saved power (0% Electricity Conserved!), but cramped backs (-3% Crew Health).
Old reactor bypass overheated coils (-5% Power) and was noisy (-3% Crew Health).
Warm bunk heat on Sol 5 helped everyone recover (+4% Crew Health).

choiceA.description: Shut down science labs and move crew to warm resting bunks.
choiceA.outcomeText: Resting helps the crew recover! Power bars hold steady.
choiceA.nasaRealDecision: Mission managers schedule rest days when astronaut fatigue gets high.
choiceA.nasaFactEmphasis: Sleep helps human brains repair and clear mental fatigue.
choiceA.guideReaction: Rest time! Cozy bunks help tired space travelers heal.

choiceB.description: Crank reactor output past normal limits to fill batteries fast.
choiceB.outcomeText: Electricity surges into batteries! Noisy pumps rattle sleeping bunks.
choiceB.nasaRealDecision: Nuclear cores can produce extra electricity by raising operating temps.
choiceB.nasaFactEmphasis: Running hot requires careful monitoring of sodium cooling valves.
choiceB.guideReaction: Power surge! The batteries fill fast, but hear that loud hum.

choiceC.description: Use power to blast static grit out of airlock door seams.
choiceC.outcomeText: Clean suitports snap shut tightly! The air blasts use modest power.
choiceC.nasaRealDecision: Suitports allow astronauts to back into suits without bringing dust inside.
choiceC.nasaFactEmphasis: Magnetic rubber gaskets seal airlock hatches against dust leaks.
choiceC.guideReaction: Whoosh! Clean seals keep every grain of dust outside.

nodes.title: Sol 6: Rover Fleet in Twilight
nodes.nasaFactBanner: 2018 LESSON: Dust devils clean solar panels, but during big storms winds stay hazy.
nodes.storyText: Cameras show heavy dust haze everywhere! We cannot count on dust devils as winds lift water vapor skyward.
nodes.guideTip: Whirlwinds on Mars sometimes sweep panels clean. Not today though!
nodes.novaHint: Rovers have big batteries. Think about linking rover power to the base.

consequences.text: Rover panel sweeps gave extra morning charge (0% Electricity Conserved!).
Orbiter communications used power (-4% Power), but Earth support lifted spirits (+5% Crew Health).
Keeping beacon mode locked preserves electricity (0% Electricity Conserved!), but dims halls (-3% Crew Health).
Shutting wing heaters saved power (0% Electricity Conserved!), but halls chilled crew (-3% Crew Health).

choiceA.description: Turn off rover heaters and dim hallway lights to save watts.
choiceA.outcomeText: Batteries gain a nice safety buffer! Dim halls make crew grumble.
choiceA.nasaRealDecision: Rovers park on high ground and sleep to save power during storms.
choiceA.nasaFactEmphasis: Parking facing the sun helps catch dawn rays when dust clears.
choiceA.guideReaction: Power saved! Dim halls, but batteries are looking healthy.

choiceB.description: Spend power heating bedrooms and scrubbing dust out of vents.
choiceB.outcomeText: Warm blankets and clean air revive crew! Battery gauges dip down.
choiceB.nasaRealDecision: Clean, warm quarters reduce stress hormones in space crews.
choiceB.nasaFactEmphasis: Deep sleep in clean air keeps cognitive reaction times high.
choiceB.guideReaction: Ahhh, warm beds and clean air! The crew feels rested.

choiceC.description: Send crew outside to wire rovers into a backup battery bank.
choiceC.outcomeText: Linked rovers feed steady power into base! Cold outdoor work tired crew.
choiceC.nasaRealDecision: NASA designs rovers with plugs to feed power back to habitats.
choiceC.nasaFactEmphasis: Rover batteries can power emergency life support for several days.
choiceC.guideReaction: Cables connected! The rovers are powering the habitat lights!

nodes.title: Sol 7: Dawn Light Breaking
nodes.nasaFactBanner: 2018 LESSON: Global dust storms begin clearing slowly after weeks of gloom.
nodes.storyText: The planet-wide storm is finally thinning! Light returns after the noon blackout. Kitchen boilers and greenhouse crops need power.
nodes.guideTip: Look at the horizon! The sky is turning from dark brown to peach!
nodes.novaHint: The storm is breaking. Decide whether to warm meals or melt water.

consequences.text: Calling Earth gave medical breathing tips and family cheers (+6% Crew Health).
Throttling chillers saved power (0% Electricity Conserved!), but crew worries about fuel (-4% Crew Health).
Warmed gym gear on Sol 5 kept muscles limber for chores (+4% Crew Health).
Sleeping rovers saved standby heat (0% Electricity Conserved!).
Dim hallway lights saved battery reserve (0% Electricity Conserved!), but slowed morning focus (-3% Crew Health).

choiceA.description: Turn off water boilers and eat dry ration bars to save power.
choiceA.outcomeText: Skipping cooking saves power! Dry cold bars leave crew sluggish.
choiceA.nasaRealDecision: Emergency ration bars provide calories without needing hot water.
choiceA.nasaFactEmphasis: Dry food bars last five years without spoiling on space missions.
choiceA.guideReaction: Crunchy ration bars! Saves power, but soup tastes better.

choiceB.description: Spend stored battery power to serve hot meals and warm water.
choiceB.outcomeText: Steaming soup restores crew strength! Battery meters dip lower.
choiceB.nasaRealDecision: Hot soup and warm drinks keep astronauts hydrated and cheerful.
choiceB.nasaFactEmphasis: Hydration is essential for preventing kidney stones in space.
choiceB.guideReaction: Hot soup time! Warm bowls make everyone feel strong again.

choiceC.description: Run underground ice drills to refill drinking water tanks.
choiceC.outcomeText: Fresh melted Martian water fills tanks! The drill motors draw power.
choiceC.nasaRealDecision: NASA will drill into glaciers beneath red dirt for pure water.
choiceC.nasaFactEmphasis: Vast sheets of water ice lie buried just a few feet underground.
choiceC.guideReaction: Fresh water tanks full! That clean ice came right from Mars.

nodes.title: Sol 7: First Sun on Dust
nodes.nasaFactBanner: 2018 LESSON: Dust devils clean panels, but static cling keeps fine grit stuck.
nodes.storyText: The planet-wide storm is thinning, but no dust devils swept panels! Thick sticky red grit still coats the glass.
nodes.guideTip: The sun is back, but the solar panels are wearing a thick dusty coat!
nodes.novaHint: Clean panels catch tomorrow's dawn sun. Decide how to clear dust.

consequences.text: Radio silence saved battery charge (0% Electricity Conserved!), but silence lowered spirits (-5% Crew Health).
Hearing voices from Earth on Sol 6 lifted crew focus for repairs (+5% Crew Health).
Skipping air scrubbing on Sol 5 left itchy dust circulating (-5% Crew Health).
Closing labs for medical care helped crew breathing (+4% Crew Health), using minor power (-3% Power).

choiceA.description: Send astronauts onto upper catwalks to sweep dust off skylights.
choiceA.outcomeText: Sunlight pours onto greenhouse plants! The spacewalk was tiring.
choiceA.nasaRealDecision: Astronauts can brush solar glass with soft conductive fiber brooms.
choiceA.nasaFactEmphasis: Sweeping off dust can double the power panels generate at dawn.
choiceA.guideReaction: Sweep sweep! Bright sunlight pours into the greenhouse.

choiceB.description: Keep crew safely inside and spend power purifying water pipes.
choiceB.outcomeText: Sparkling clean water refreshes the team! Panels stay dusty for now.
choiceB.nasaRealDecision: The space station recycles 98% of all water through high-tech filters.
choiceB.nasaFactEmphasis: Recycled space water is cleaner than most municipal tap water on Earth.
choiceB.guideReaction: Pure fresh water! Staying inside keeps everyone safe and dry.

choiceC.description: Pulse mechanical vibrators on solar wings to shake off dust.
choiceC.outcomeText: Clouds of red grit slide off panels! The buzzing rattles the walls.
choiceC.nasaRealDecision: Engineers test ultrasonic buzzers to shake dust off solar arrays.
choiceC.nasaFactEmphasis: Rapid shaking breaks the static bond holding dry grit to glass.
choiceC.guideReaction: Bzzzzt! Look at all that dust slide off the solar wings!

nodes.title: Sol 7: Sick Bay Alert
nodes.nasaFactBanner: 2018 LESSON: Humans need clean oxygen to live, while robot rovers do not breathe.
nodes.storyText: In 2018, Curiosity rolled safely without lungs, but our crew feels strain! Spend power on MOXIE oxygen and airlock seals.
nodes.guideTip: Astronaut lungs need clean air. Breathing red dust is no fun!
nodes.novaHint: Crew health is critical. Clean the sick bay air or enforce masks.

consequences.text: Redlining reactor on Sol 6 strained valves (-5% Power) and was noisy (-3% Crew Health).
Rebooting greenhouse used power (-4% Power), but fresh greens revived crew (+5% Crew Health).
Clogged filters from Sol 4 let fine dust into sleeping bunks (-5% Crew Health).
Warming bunks and scrubbers restored crew stamina (+4% Crew Health), using power (-4% Power).

choiceA.description: Run emergency high-speed scrubbers to clean medical room air.
choiceA.outcomeText: Emergency scrubbers clear stale air! Battery banks are sharply drained.
choiceA.nasaRealDecision: Medical bays on space stations maintain positive air pressure for healing.
choiceA.nasaFactEmphasis: Clean air helps human airways heal quickly from mineral irritation.
choiceA.guideReaction: Pure clean air in sick bay! Astronauts can breathe easy.

choiceB.description: Save electricity by having tired crew wear breathing helmets inside.
choiceB.outcomeText: Power meters hold steady! Wearing heavy helmets inside tires everyone.
choiceB.nasaRealDecision: Sealed breathing masks protect astronauts during cabin contamination.
choiceB.nasaFactEmphasis: Filtered respirators block fine particles down to 0.3 microns.
choiceB.guideReaction: Helmets on indoors! Saves power, but helmets are heavy.

choiceC.description: Lock down dirty lab rooms to keep bedroom air clean and calm.
choiceC.outcomeText: Sealing the lab gives lungs relief! The quiet filters use modest power.
choiceC.nasaRealDecision: Isolating dusty modules prevents grit from spreading through ventilation.
choiceC.nasaFactEmphasis: Closing compartment doors contains airborne dust to a single zone.
choiceC.guideReaction: Dusty lab sealed! Bedroom air stays fresh and clean.

nodes.title: Sol 7: Satellites Spot Dawn
nodes.nasaFactBanner: 2018 LESSON: Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter tracked the 2018 storm from high above.
nodes.storyText: Cameras look murky, like on Curiosity's dusty selfie! An orbital satellite passes across the 22-minute radio delay.
nodes.guideTip: The orbiter can see where the storm clouds are breaking up!
nodes.novaHint: Sunlight is returning soon. Check orbiter maps or warm up turbines.

consequences.text: Weather drone mapped flat paths, saving rover power today (0% Electricity Conserved!).
Linking rover batteries supplied extra watts (0% Electricity Conserved!), but crowded floors (-3% Crew Health).
Earlier rover panel sweeps harvest faint twilight charge (0% Electricity Conserved!).
Flushing airlock suitports cleared grit (+3% Crew Health), using power (-3% Power).

choiceA.description: Pull rover batteries into base and scrape gritty outer cable plugs.
choiceA.outcomeText: Rover battery reserves boost base power! Cold airlock repairs tired crew.
choiceA.nasaRealDecision: Technicians use copper brushes to clear grit from electrical contacts.
choiceA.nasaFactEmphasis: Clean electrical contacts prevent voltage drops across power cords.
choiceA.guideReaction: Plugs cleaned! Rover batteries give the habitat extra power.

choiceB.description: Send power to outdoor turbine heaters while crew eats cold rations.
choiceB.outcomeText: Warmed turbines produce steady power! Cold snacks make crew grumpy.
choiceB.nasaRealDecision: Heating mechanical bearings keeps lubricant fluid in subzero air.
choiceB.nasaFactEmphasis: Frozen grease can seize rotating turbine shafts completely.
choiceB.guideReaction: Turbines warm! Steady power flows, but hot food would be nice.

choiceC.description: Spend dish power linking with orbiters to map thinning dust clouds.
choiceC.outcomeText: Orbital maps show sunlight returning soon! Crew morale shoots up.
choiceC.nasaRealDecision: High-altitude color cameras photograph dust thinning across Mars.
choiceC.nasaFactEmphasis: Tracking thinning dust tells astronauts when to resume outdoor science.
choiceC.guideReaction: Good news from space! Sunlight is breaking through the clouds.
